title: Improve presbyopic near vision with approved eye drops

concept.text: Provide clinically useful temporary improvement in near vision through pharmacological treatment. Pupil-modulating drops achieved this endpoint without establishing restoration of youthful accommodation. Proposed completion test: FDA approval supported by randomized phase 3 trials showing more participants gain at least three lines of mesopic binocular distance-corrected near visual acuity without losing more than five distance-vision letters, assessed at the prespecified post-dose time. Test set by: FDA; GEMINI efficacy assessments used day 30, hour 3. Reported achieved: FDA approved pilocarpine 1.25% (Vuity) on 29 October 2021. Sources given: [FDA Vuity clinical review](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2022/214028Orig1s000SumR.pdf) ; [Manufacturer's dated approval announcement](https://news.abbvie.com/2021-10-29-U-S-Food-and-Drug-Administration-Approves-VUITY-TM-pilocarpine-HCI-ophthalmic-solution-1-25-%2C-the-First-and-Only-Eye-Drop-to-Treat-Presbyopia-Age-Related-Blurry-Near-Vision).

page.title: First eye drop approved to treat presbyopia
page.definition: A regulator approves an eye drop that temporarily improves near vision in adults with presbyopia, the age-related loss of the eye’s ability to focus on nearby objects. The breakthrough is the first such approval. It does not require an effect that lasts the whole day or the return of accommodation, the lens’s change of focus.

goal.need: A 2018 systematic review and model estimated that the global unmet need for presbyopia correction in 2015 was 45% (95% confidence interval, 41%–49%).

figures.caption: Estimated global burden of presbyopia in 2015
rows: People with near-vision impairment from absent or inadequate correction

statements.quote: Thus, there remains a need for improved methods for correcting presbyopia.
statements.context: Background section of FDA’s review of Vuity.

statements.quote: The overall objective of this clinical development program is to develop a fixed-dose combination of oxymetazoline and pilocarpine for the treatment of presbyopia.
statements.context: Development objective for the combination eye-drop candidate in protocol 199201-010.

completion.title: FDA approves an eye drop for the treatment of presbyopia in adults.
completion.criterion: The US Food and Drug Administration approves an ophthalmic solution with the indication of treating presbyopia in adults, on the basis of two randomized, double-masked, vehicle-controlled phase 3 trials. In each, more participants on the drop than on vehicle gain 3 lines or more in mesopic (dim-light), high-contrast, binocular distance-corrected near visual acuity without losing more than 1 line (5 letters) of corrected distance acuity. The first such approval was Vuity (pilocarpine hydrochloride 1.25%), one drop in each eye once daily, on 28 October 2021: 750 participants aged 40 to 55; at day 30, hour 3, responders were 31% versus 8% and 26% versus 11%.
completion.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, NDA 214028 approval letter, Vuity prescribing information section 14 and cross-discipline team leader review.
completion.threshold_quote: There are currently no approved therapeutic products in the US for presbyopia.
completion.basis: The entry is narrowed to the first approval, which the FDA review records as a first. The primary endpoint was read 3 hours after a dose, and 26% and 31% of treated participants met it. The test sets no duration of effect and does not ask that reading glasses become unnecessary through the day. Longer-acting drops and treatments that restore accommodation are outside this test.

milestones.title: A presbyopia drop has nonclinical evidence sufficient for initial testing in people.
milestones.criterion: Nonclinical data and previous human experience support a finding that a candidate drop is reasonably safe for initial human testing. Vuity’s programme included rabbit study TX13119, begun on 25 November 2013: unilateral pilocarpine 1% plus oxymetazoline 0.05%–0.25%, twice daily for 30 days, caused no adverse ocular toxicity. FDA found the overall nonclinical package acceptable on 22 October 2021.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, Investigational New Drug Application guidance; Vuity’s nonclinical findings are documented in its regulatory reviews.
milestones.threshold_quote: Nonclinical data to permit an assessment as to whether the product is reasonably safe for initial testing in humans.

milestones.title: A presbyopia drop produces a two-line near-acuity gain at most tested times in an early human study.
milestones.criterion: Study 199201-007 defined response as gaining at least two lines in dim-light, high-contrast uncorrected near acuity in the nondominant eye at a majority of postdose measurements, at least three, relative to the first predose measurement. The study treated 65 participants with pilocarpine 1%, oxymetazoline 0.125%, or both. Allergan’s protocol dated 4 April 2016 reports a statistically greater responder proportion with once-daily pilocarpine than vehicle. This is a sponsor protocol summary, not a peer-reviewed result.
milestones.set_by: Allergan, study 199201-007 responder definition, reproduced in protocol 199201-009; this threshold belongs to that early study.

milestones.title: A presbyopia drop shows a near-acuity dose response at the protocol’s two-sided P ≤ 0.05 threshold.
milestones.criterion: Study 199201-009 assessed weighted average changes in uncorrected near-acuity letters in the nondominant eye over two-day dosing periods, hours 1–10. Its significance threshold was two-sided P ≤ 0.05, without adjustment for multiple tests. The phase 2 study enrolled 163 participants; 157 entered the modified intention-to-treat analysis. Pilocarpine showed a dose response, P < 0.001; oxymetazoline did not, P = 0.4797. Results were published on 2 October 2021.
milestones.set_by: Allergan, protocol 199201-009, sections 7.2 and 7.3; this statistical threshold belongs to that dose-ranging study.
milestones.threshold_quote: A 2-sided test with a p-value ≤ 0.05 will be considered statistically significant.

milestones.title: A presbyopia drop enters phase 3 testing under an effective investigational new drug application.
milestones.criterion: An investigational new drug application becomes effective 30 days after FDA receipt unless FDA imposes a clinical hold, or following earlier FDA notification permitting investigation. Human dosing also requires the applicable ethics approvals. The published GEMINI 1 protocol identifies IND 122483; the peer-reviewed report documents ethics approval at each site and commencement of the phase 3 study on 21 December 2018.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 312.40; GEMINI 1 supplies the documented clinical-development example.
milestones.threshold_quote: An investigator may not administer an investigational new drug to human subjects until the IND goes into effect

milestones.title: A presbyopia drop beats vehicle on the three-line near-acuity response in two phase 3 studies.
milestones.criterion: In GEMINI 1 and GEMINI 2, responders gain at least three lines in dim-light, high-contrast binocular distance-corrected near acuity at day 30, three hours after dosing, without losing more than five corrected-distance-acuity letters using the same correction. The responder proportion must exceed vehicle at two-sided P < 0.05. Across 750 adults aged 40–55 years receiving pilocarpine 1.25% or vehicle once daily for 30 days, FDA’s 2021 label reports 31% versus 8% in GEMINI 1, n = 163 versus 160, and 26% versus 11% in GEMINI 2, n = 212 versus 215; both P < 0.01.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, original Vuity prescribing information, section 14, with the significance level specified in Allergan’s GEMINI protocols; this is the Vuity programme’s test.
milestones.threshold_quote: gaining 3 lines or more in mesopic, high contrast, binocular distance corrected near visual acuity (DCNVA)

not_found: The public FDA nonclinical review does not disclose animal group sizes for rabbit study TX13119.
A separate public FDA letter establishing the effective date of IND 122483 was not located.

results.finding: Rabbit study TX13119 (sample size not stated) found no adverse ocular toxicity after 30 days of pilocarpine/oxymetazoline dosing.
results.detail: Unilateral pilocarpine 1% plus oxymetazoline 0.05%–0.25% was administered twice daily. FDA concluded that the NDA was approvable from a nonclinical pharmacology/toxicology perspective; the review was signed on 22 October 2021.
results.quote:
Unilateral ocular instillation of pilocarpine (1%) / oxymetazoline (0.05% - 0.25%), 
BID for 30 days, did not cause adverse toxicity in the rabbit eye

results.finding: Pilocarpine plus oxymetazoline in rabbits (5–7 per sex per group) produced no adverse histopathology after 28 days.
results.detail: The sponsor reports nonclinical safety support and prior human experience, but does not document the specified 30-day TX13119 study or FDA's finding that the overall nonclinical package was acceptable.
results.quote: No histopathological findings were observed in any treatment group.

results.finding: Study 199201-007 (65 participants): once-daily pilocarpine significantly exceeded vehicle for ≥2-line near-acuity response at most postdose times.
results.detail: Response required improvement in mesopic, high-contrast uncorrected near acuity in the nondominant eye at at least three postdose measurements. This is a sponsor protocol summary; no responder percentage or exact P value is provided.
results.quote:
Pilocarpine monotherapy provided a statistically significant greater response over vehicle in 
the percentage of patients achieving at least a 2 line improvement in mesopic, high-contrast 
UNV A at a majority of time points postdose in the nondominant eye following QD dosing

results.finding: In the extended phase 2 study (n=151), the Medium OU group showed significant two-line near-acuity improvement through 8 hours.
results.detail: This study reports responder proportions separately at each time point, not the required participant-level response at a majority of measurements. It is not study 199201-007 and does not establish its specified responder endpoint.
results.quote: The Medium OU group was the only group to have a statistically significant percentage of participants maintain 2-line improvement at every time point on day 28 from 0.5 to 8 hours.

results.finding: Pilocarpine showed a near-acuity dose response in the short-term phase 2 study (163 enrolled; 157 mITT), P < 0.001.
results.detail: The endpoint averaged change in mesopic, high-contrast uncorrected near-acuity letters in the nondominant eye over two-day dosing periods. Oxymetazoline showed no significant dose response (P = 0.4797).
results.quote:
In the short-term study, Pilo was shown to produce a significant dose response in the average increase of letters (
P
< 0.001), whereas Oxy did not have a significant impact (
P =
0.4797).

results.finding: GEMINI 1 enrolled 323 participants in phase 3 testing beginning 21 December 2018.
results.detail: The report documents phase 3 commencement and ethics approval at each site. The supplied text does not identify IND 122483 or establish that the IND was effective.
results.quote: The GEMINI 1 study was a 30-day, multicenter, double-masked, randomized, vehicle-controlled, parallel-group, phase 3 trial conducted at 36 sites in the United States from December 21, 2018, to October 31, 2019, in compliance with the Declaration of Helsinki.

results.finding: GEMINI 1 (n=323): AGN-190584 increased the three-line near-acuity responder proportion over vehicle by 22.5 percentage points.
results.detail: At day 30, hour 3, responders were 30.7% versus 8.1% (adjusted P<.001). No responder lost more than five corrected-distance letters in a post hoc analysis. Only GEMINI 1 is reported; the criterion requires both GEMINI 1 and GEMINI 2.
results.quote: On day 30, hour 3, the percentage of participants with improvement of 3 or more lines in mesopic DCNVA was 30.7% (50 of 163) in the AGN-190584 group and 8.1% (13 of 160) in the vehicle group

results.finding: VUITY exceeded vehicle on the three-line near-acuity response in GEMINI 1 and GEMINI 2 (750 participants total; both P < 0.01).
results.detail: At day 30, hour 3, response rates were 31% versus 8% (n=163 versus 160) and 26% versus 11% (n=212 versus 215). Response required mesopic, high-contrast binocular DCNVA gain of at least three lines without losing more than five CDVA letters using the same correction.

results.finding: FDA labeling establishes VUITY 1.25% for adult presbyopia, supported by two randomized phase 3 trials totaling 750 participants.
results.detail: The official label specifies one drop in each eye once daily and records efficacy in both vehicle-controlled trials. The electronic record was signed on 28 October 2021.
results.quote: VUITY is indicated for the treatment of presbyopia in adults.

results.finding: FDA approved Vuity (pilocarpine hydrochloride 1.25%) for presbyopia in adults on 28 October 2021; sample size not reported.
results.detail: The signed FDA letter establishes approval. The supplied text does not report the supporting trials’ sample sizes or efficacy results.
results.quote:
We have completed our review of this application, as amended. It is approved, effective 
on the date of this letter, for use as recommended in the enclosed agreed-upon 
labeling.

results.finding: Once-daily pilocarpine in 17 participants produced a two-line near-acuity response at most postdose measurements in 70.6%.
results.detail: Clinical Study A uses the specified dim-light, high-contrast, nondominant-eye endpoint and first predose baseline. However, this patent does not identify study 199201-007, report its 65-participant total, or establish a statistically greater responder proportion than vehicle.
results.quote:
the percentage of patients achieving the primary endpoint, at least a 2-line improvement from baseline in mesopic, high contrast UNVA (hour 0 of visit 1) in the non-dominant eye at a majority (at least 3) of time points post dose
was 70.6%.

results.finding: Pilocarpine entered phase 3 testing in GEMINI 1 (322 treated participants); the FDA review identifies IND 122483.
results.detail: The review documents phase 3 dosing, GCP compliance and meetings under IND 122483, but does not establish when the IND became effective, site ethics approvals or the 21 December 2018 start date.
results.quote:
This was a multicenter, double-masked, randomized, parallel-group, vehicle-controlled, Phase 3 
study in participants with presbyopia.  Participants received AGN-190584 1.25% or vehicle 
dosed once daily, bilaterally, for 30 days.

results.finding: Pilocarpine 1.25% beat vehicle on the specified near-acuity response in two phase 3 trials (750 randomized adults); both P < 0.0001.
results.detail: Studies 301/302 used once-daily dosing for 30 days in adults aged 40–55 and the specified day-30, hour-3 endpoint, including the distance-acuity safeguard. Responses were 30.7% vs 8.1% and 26.0% vs 10.8%. Study 302 excluded 28 participants for incorrect baseline measurements; including them still gave P = 0.00015.
results.quote:
The p-values from the
Chi-squared test were < 0.0001 in both studies.
